name: Sarban core - the engine says what it knows

stages.title: Telegram actually delivers
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC1. Root cause is cited there: nothing ever starts the hosted service - RunCommand resolves the Orchestrator straight from the container, so _started stays false and every push is silently dropped while the test button works. Follow the ControlPlaneServer precedent of an explicit start. Acceptance: a real run path delivers a real push, two-way answers, and a regression test drives the actual run-start path. The live proof is a nested run of YOUR build against a scratch repo (promptExtra trap 2) - CONDUCTOR_TELEGRAM_TOKEN must be present in your environment; the owner sets it before launch. If the token is genuinely absent, record a HUMAN: line and park - never mock the push to claim.

stages.title: Truthful surfaces
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC2. Status never calls a healthy run interrupted; sticky failure fields age or clear; one canonical gates GREEN or RED vocabulary on phase-gate lines plus an honest no-gates-configured confirmation state and consistent attempt numbering; /state carries in-flight and window-vs-lifetime spend; RUN-SUMMARY.md on completion, offline report and status, shared-read log, incremental SSE tails.

stages.title: Config traps die at authoring time
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC3. Doctor FAILS on a dropped model token; unknown RunIf and SkipIf tokens fail at plan load; plan set refuses absent leaf keys, suggests the dotted path, and reaches the live engine or says how; a literal brace in plan prose is caught by doctor and parks at runtime instead of a silent stderr-only exit, with a double-brace escape; advisor defaults work headless or refuse loudly, and plan-config.md stops documenting a default that does not exist.

stages.title: Verdicts judge the work, not the environment
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC4. Settle before the battery and retry a red required gate once before GatesRed; NoProgress requires no commits AND no newly-DONE checkpoints, with conductor's own chore commits excluded from the count; satelliteRepos for multi-repo diffs and gate-cache keys that cover the gate's own working directory and command text; injections render at the top of the prompt and supersede a stale gate-failures block.

stages.title: The engine can wait, detach, and correct the board
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC5. Blocked-until as a first-class session outcome the run loop honours by sleeping and respawning once, surfaced everywhere; run --detach prints pid and control-plane url and survives its launching shell; task --todo --blocked --skipped --amend land through the shared writes path and --in-progress reports the post-fold truth; bg rows map to their session stream and runtimes use one timezone. Prove detach and blocked-until with YOUR build against a scratch repo (promptExtra trap 2) - never by aiming run verbs at this repo.

stages.title: Clean history without lying about it
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC6. Pure status-transition commits stop landing; any squash runs AFTER the final state write, works on a dirty tree, reports real counts, logs git stderr and exit code on failure, un-marks the stage on failure instead of permanently marking it squashed, aborts a half-started rebase, and degrades gracefully off Windows.

stages.title: The transcript captures structure
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC7. Store tool events structured - name plus extracted fields, values truncated, JSON never cut - with back-compat reading of the old lines; note writes outside the repo in the verdict; emit readable one-liner wire lines from the provider and compute, store and serve a per-session digest. The worked example in the spec is the acceptance shape. This stage enables the whole face round.

stages.title: The program knows what it is and can update itself
stages.notes: SPEC: docs/history/CONDUCTOR-SARBAN.md section SC8. A version verb and /version endpoint stamped at build with semver, git sha and date; automatic tag-height versioning reconciled with the release workflow so a downloaded binary answers with its tag; install.ps1 prints before and after versions; CHANGELOG per release; conductor update checks the latest release and swaps binaries safely, refusing while a run is live; doctor reports update-available. Prove the swap against a scratch copy of an installed engine - never the live published one driving you (promptExtra traps 1 and 2).

gates.name: face-fast
gates.command: cmd /c "cd /d C:\code\conductor\face-go && go build ./... && go vet ./..."

promptExtra:
TRAPS THIS REPO HAS ALREADY PAID FOR, in order of cost:
1. NEVER run tools/install.ps1 or overwrite the published engine - the conductor driving you runs from that published copy. The owner reinstalls between plans.
2. This repo's .conductor/ is the LIVE state of the run driving you. The claim and note verbs (conductor task, note, bug, bg) and read-only verbs (status, task --list) are yours; NEVER aim run-control verbs (run, pause, resume, abort, approve, plan set, plan reload, goto, skip, retry-stage, rollback, kill) at this repo. Any live-run proof spawns YOUR build against a scratch repo with its own tiny plan and its own .conductor - for example under %TEMP%\sarban-proofs - never against C:/code/conductor.
3. The conductor on PATH is the OLD published engine - the one driving you. Exercise YOUR changes through the fresh build: dotnet run --project src/Conductor -- VERB, or the exe it builds. Testing a new verb through the PATH shim only proves the old engine lacks it. Exception by design: task claims go through the PATH copy, because they target the driving run.
4. The ratchet gate is tools/gates/ratchet.ps1 - the wrong path prints an error but exits 0, a silent false green. Never raise the pragma ceiling; fix the cause instead, as DoctorCommand's AsyncCommand conversion did.
5. face-go: pad plain text then style, never width-format an ANSI string; clamp with MaxWidth and MaxHeight; goldens pin UTC and live in face-go/internal/tui/testdata/golden - regenerate them in a separate rebaseline commit, and read face-go/STYLE.md before any face change.
6. Orphaned dotnet test hosts flake the full suite; stopping stray dotnet processes between full runs is sanctioned, but never kill the conductor process itself.
7. PowerShell tooling targets Windows PowerShell 5.1 and must stay ASCII-only - em-dashes have torn string literals here before.
8. Keep tracker handoffs, checkpoint titles and all plan prose free of curly braces - a literal brace token reaches the composed prompt and kills the CURRENT engine at the stage boundary. SC3.3 fixes this; until the owner reinstalls the fixed engine, the discipline stands.
9. The conductor MCP task tools may arrive deferred in your harness - ToolSearch for task_update first, or use the CLI: conductor task --done ID --evidence PATH. That command is the only claim; prose moves nothing.
10. Commit per checkpoint with the repo's trailer convention and push feat/sarban. Go sources are checked out LF; keep them that way.

deliver.name: deliver
deliver.description: Deliver until the stage's checkpoints are confirmed; fix only when gates are red.
